keyPoints: daily-api runs on a Flex Consumption (FC1) plan, replacing the unsupported Linux Y1 plan in the resource group.
Python 3.12 runtime is configured for daily-api, with enhanced scaling (40 max instances) and memory allocation (2048 MB per instance).
A deployment blob container (`app-package-daily-api-prod`) is introduced, with a `DEPLOYMENT_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` setting for deployment storage.
daily-api retains its own storage account, App Insights instance, and Azure Table Storage tables (DailyChecklist, DailyLinks, DailyCards).
architecture.overview: The Azure infrastructure is defined using modular Bicep files deployed at subscription scope. Each service has its own module. The daily-api module now provisions a Flex Consumption (FC1) plan, ensuring compatibility with the resource group and supporting Python 3.12 runtime. Deployment storage is configured via a dedicated blob container, enabling efficient deployment workflows. Posts-api continues to temporarily reference daily-api's storage connection string until its daily routes are fully migrated.

sections.heading: Features

sections.content: The Azure infrastructure is defined using modular Bicep files deployed at subscription scope. Each service has its own module. The Container App Environment module creates the shared Log Analytics workspace used for unified observability across all Container Apps. The arch-content-foundry module provisions an OpenAI resource with a GPT-4o deployment for the arch-content-update CI workflow. The gpt-5.3-codex model for ideas-bot is deployed independently to avoid quota-related deployment failures impacting the rest of the infrastructure. Additionally, Azure Table Storage is provisioned and utilized by ideas-api for project resolution and backfill operations, ensuring robust data consistency and integrity for project and idea management workflows. Posts-api integrates with history-api for version-history storage, requiring HISTORY_API_URL and HISTORY_API_KEY environment variables to enable secure communication.
sections.heading: Architecture

sections.content:
- Subscription-scope deployment — all resources land in a single resource group
- Managed Identity role assignments are defined alongside the resources that need them
- Container Registry uses admin credentials (not Managed Identity) for simplicity
- Log Analytics workspace is shared by momentum-finder, trail-finder, and dashboard-api
- Scaling rules on Container Apps: min 0 replicas (scale to zero), max 10
- arch-content-foundry OpenAI resource uses GlobalStandard SKU with 50K TPM capacity
- gpt-5.3-codex model for ideas-bot is deployed separately to mitigate quota constraints
- Azure Table Storage is used by ideas-api for project resolution and backfill operations, supporting features like name-based project linkage and one-time data backfill scripts
- history-api runs on a Flex Consumption plan, required for Go-based Azure Functions during public preview
- history-api uses EasyAuth with an App Registration for secure authentication and authorization
- Dedicated storage account for history-api includes versions table and history-attachments blob container
- posts-api integrates with history-api for version-history storage, requiring HISTORY_API_URL and HISTORY_API_KEY environment variables
